title: Your First Project Folder and Safe Working Habits
learningObjectives: Explain the main ideas in your own words
Apply the workflow to a small project
Identify mistakes and correct them safely

understand.concept: A project folder keeps the files for one website together. Begin with a clear root folder and separate folders for styles, scripts and images. Keep a known starting page such as index.html at the root unless the project structure requires otherwise.
understand.whyItMatters: Use descriptive filenames, save changes often, keep a backup or version history, and avoid placing passwords, private keys or personal data in files that may be published. Only use assets you created or have permission to use.
understand.history: This lesson focuses on current, practical web-development concepts; historical claims are omitted where they are not needed.
understand.analogy: A project folder is like a labelled work area: tools and materials have predictable places. The comparison does not mean every project must use the same folder layout; choose a structure that fits its size and explain it consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a learning aid, not a complete description of technical behaviour.

explain.narrative:
A project folder keeps the files for one website together. Begin with a clear root folder and separate folders for styles, scripts and images. Keep a known starting page such as index.html at the root unless the project structure requires otherwise.

Use descriptive filenames, save changes often, keep a backup or version history, and avoid placing passwords, private keys or personal data in files that may be published. Only use assets you created or have permission to use.

A project folder is like a labelled work area: tools and materials have predictable places. The comparison does not mean every project must use the same folder layout; choose a structure that fits its size and explain it consistently.
